ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Dominantly low-intensity (black) surface area with localized high-intensity (white) reflectance points. High-intensity pixels comprise approximately 5-8% of the total visible ventral fluke surface.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Base substrate is a continuous black field. High-contrast white mapping includes: (1) scattered focal clusters across both lobes; (2) a dense grouping of horizontal linear streaks on the right lobe; (3) solid high-intensity patches at the extreme lateral distal tips.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped central notch with an approximate interior angle of 85 degrees; the vertex is sharply defined with a bounding box depth of approximately 45 pixels.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Continuous high-frequency serration along the trailing edge boundary. Variations exhibit greater pixel-amplitude (peaks) at the outer thirds of both lobes, reaching up to 12 pixels from the mean edge trajectory, while the medial sections are relatively smoother.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Symmetric bilateral lobes showing an initial slight convexity from the median notch, followed by an aggressive upward concavity (sweep) towards the distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Dozens of localized, circular high-contrast white pixel clusters (varying 2-6 pixels in diameter) distributed across both lobes, characteristic of barnacle attachment points or scars.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: A series of at least four distinct, unaligned horizontal white linear streaks on the right lobe, appearing as high-contrast disruptions against the dark pigmentation.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Presence of multiple linear rake marks on the right lobe and significant irregular tissue indentations along the superior trailing edge, particularly at the distal margins.
other_distinctive_markers: Highly distinctive white pigmentation caps at the extreme terminal tips of both the left and right lobes.
